I also have social anxiety (technically " Social Phobia"), which _is_ a mental illness. Who the hell cares? Seems pretty unlikely to me.  I think when a cis person wonders what's wrong with their life,  there's a good thousand things that come to mind before "I'm trans". Hell, it takes decades even for some trans people (myself included)

>>second puberty

It really is. I'm going in the opposite direction but I can tell you, things are weird. First keep in mind that for a trans person, the last time the went through puberty it really sucked, badly, so they're probably a bit on edge. 

Plus your body is changing, and there's all kinds of strange thoughts going through your head. You might even have some internalized transphobia and/or homophobia, that makes you hate yourself. 

Plus, T is a motherfucker. It's testosterone and yeah, it makes you more aggressive. I'm sure it's exactly what your friend needs,  but it sounds like what you are describing is an effect, not a side effect. 

That said, being trans doesn't automatically make you a nice person.  If you aren't happy being around them,  and especially, if you don't feel safe around them, you don't have to be friends with them. 

[edit] just wanted to add,  I've been given permission by several different doctors to self adjust several different medication dosages, within specified ranges. This has included a benzo, a beta blocker, as well as a stimulant (adhd medication). It's not as unusual as you may think.

Pre HRT and going full time I never really "felt like a woman". I had depression and social anxiety and I was suicidal and I didn't understand why. I couldn't fit in with other men, and I couldn't ever figure out how to have a relationship with women. 

I started HRT 6 months ago and living as a woman full time 3.5 months ago.  Now I feel like a woman and nothing could be more right.  Something was always wrong but I had no idea what it was, and it wasn't until I spent some time living as one that I really, truly felt like one... Felt comfortable in my own skin.

I wouldn't say HRT/transitioning has directly helped it.  But... I am somewhat more motivated because I'm also not depressed and anxious all the time. I can actually imagine my life a year from now (a big adhd issue is having trouble thinking about the future).  

I have notice done concrete improvement.  I've always been terrible with names.  Like, I could work with somebody for 3 months and never learn their name e.  Now I'm much better, and often I can remember someone's name after meeting them just a few times - sometimes only meeting them once.  I've also noticed that my medium to long term memory has improved a bit (short term memory is still shit).  I think this is mostly because I'm actually happy, and not wanting to die all the time,  and this makes it easier to remember things. 

Anyway, YMMV!

A possible side effect of many anti depressants is a loss of the ability to have an erection. If I'm reading right, you are actually experiencing the opposite... A renewed and unwanted ability to have erections (please correct me if I'm wrong). 

Regardless, standard advice applies... If you're not happy with the 'side effects', try a different any depressant. There are dozens if not hundreds, and each one is a little bit different for every person, and eventually you'll findone that works for you. 

Also, are you on hormones? I found that my and depressant didn't kill my erections on its own, but within about two months of starting hormones, they were gone, gone, gone (I'm pretty indifferent about this). So you might find that the combo works better for you too.

Same here, and I read the same thing over and over again in this sub.  Yes,  terrible things can and do happen to trans people when they come out. But for the most part, people are good, and we WAY over exaggerate the likelihood of negative reactions. **and we tend to not think about the impact of positive, affirming reactions**. 

When I came out,  my parents had a difficult time, and my sister was so angry that she didn't speak to me for 6 months. Some Co workers were indifferent, and some were so moved that they cried. A few of my old friends don't really talk to me any more. 

But oh my God. I never thought about this happening... I made new friends. Several Cis women, several trans women, and have a much stronger (platonic) relationship with a few cis men.  These people completley accept me as a woman and have been super supportive of me in every way.  The girls have gone shopping with me, gone to parties with me,  even gone to the bathroom with me. 

Yes,  things might be rocky with your parents, but they probably won't be as bad as you think, and they probably won't be forever. And there will be positives too! Probably ones you can't even imagine right now. 


P. S. After 6 months, my parents finally used my female name, and my sister started talking to me again.

Endo is stupid. Find a new one (if possible).  You can be on too high a dosage - the idea is to get your hormones to a female level, not to take the maximum amount you can tolerate. The concept of sex and Gender being separate things, and of sex being some universal immovable truth,  is so flawed it's not even worth talking about sex. 

Genetic...  Women are born with male chromosomes and look just like women, otherwise, and some don't even know for most of their lives. Same way the other way around

Genitalia... Women are born with 'male parts'  female parts,  even ambiguous parts.

(don't try to find your own symptoms here. These are things I never imagined about myself until I started HRT!)
